copyright_boundary: These are original procedural summaries. They identify public W3C sources but do not reproduce normative standard text.
usage_rule: Use a listed procedure only after fixing the target scope and opening its primary sources. This partial catalog covers only the listed criteria; it does not make an unlisted criterion executable or the profile complete.

applicability_steps: Inventory each user-presented non-text item in the fixed scope, including images, SVGs, icons, image controls, charts, audio, video, CAPTCHA, and decorative assets.
Classify the item's purpose from its visible context and operation: informative, functional or input, time-based media, test, sensory experience, CAPTCHA, or decorative/formatting/invisible.
Record the classification rationale and identify items whose purpose changes after interaction or with a changed state.
procedure_steps: For every applicable item, inspect the computed programmatic name, text alternative, adjacent equivalent text, or intentional mechanism that hides decoration from assistive technology.

Compare the inspected alternative with the information, action, state, or trend that the item conveys in the fixed target state; inspect a data table or prose alternative when a short label cannot carry equivalent chart or diagram information.

For image controls and input, exercise the permitted action and confirm that the accessible name describes the control purpose; record separately any related requirements that are outside this criterion.
For exceptions, verify the applicable exception conditions rather than treating the presence of an attribute as a result.
expected_results: Each applicable informative item has a text alternative that serves the equivalent purpose and conveys the needed information in its context.
Each applicable functional item has a programmatic name that describes its purpose, and decorative content is ignored by assistive technology rather than announced as meaningless content.
Items falling within an explicit exception have the descriptive identification or alternate modality appropriate to that exception.
cant_tell_when: The item's purpose, visible context, state-dependent meaning, or computed alternative cannot be observed in the permitted scope.
A complex chart, diagram, media item, CAPTCHA, or third-party asset cannot be compared with an equivalent text alternative or exception conditions.

pass: A chart has a concise label plus nearby text or a data table that communicates the same trend and values needed to use the chart.
A decorative icon is intentionally hidden from assistive technology while its adjacent text already conveys the only meaning.
fail: An informative chart is exposed only as a generic name such as 'image' or a filename, with no equivalent trend or data in text.
An image control has no programmatic name that describes what activating it does.
cant_tell: A screenshot shows an SVG label, but the reviewer cannot inspect its computed name or determine whether the visible data is fully available elsewhere in text.

procedures.ai_boundary: AI may inventory candidate non-text items or draft questions, but it must not record a profile outcome, human_verified mapping, or E2+ claim; an external human reviewer records any criterion result with target-specific evidence.

applicability_steps: Identify information, structure, and relationships conveyed through visual or auditory presentation in the fixed scope, including headings, lists, landmarks, tables, labels, required indicators, grouped fields, and state or status cues.
Identify relationships that are necessary to understand or operate the content when visual styling, position, grouping, color, or sound is unavailable.
Record any content or technology where relationships can only be checked through a linearized view or accessibility tree.
procedure_steps: Inspect the DOM, accessibility tree, or equivalent programmatic structure and compare it with the visible relationships in the same target state.

Check that headings, lists, tables, form labels, grouped controls, regions, and other applicable structures expose the relationships necessary for understanding or operation, or that an equivalent text statement is available near the content.
Review the content in a linearized or assistive-technology-facing representation when needed to determine whether the relationship survives presentation changes.
Record the exact visual relationship, programmatic or textual representation, and any unresolved boundary rather than inferring a result from tag presence alone.
expected_results: Information, structure, and relationships conveyed through presentation are programmatically determined or available in text for the scoped content.
Relationships needed to interpret tables, form fields, grouped controls, headings, lists, and regions remain available when presentation changes.
Semantic markup represents the actual content relationship rather than merely producing a visual effect.
cant_tell_when: The relevant relationship cannot be compared between the visual presentation and the DOM, accessibility tree, or linearized representation.
Dynamic or third-party content prevents the reviewer from determining whether the necessary relationship is programmatically determined or available in text.

pass: A data table exposes its row and column headers so that a data cell can be associated with the relevant headers.
A required-field indicator is explained in text and associated with the appropriate form fields rather than conveyed only by presentation.
fail: Visual headings are only bold paragraphs, with no programmatic heading or nearby text that conveys the section structure.
A table-like layout uses visual columns but does not expose the header-to-cell relationships needed to interpret its values.
cant_tell: A static screenshot suggests a grouped form or data table, but the reviewer cannot inspect its accessibility tree, linearized content, or source relationships.

procedures.ai_boundary: AI may inventory candidate relationships or draft questions, but it must not record a profile outcome, human_verified mapping, or E2+ claim; an external human reviewer records any criterion result with target-specific evidence.

applicability_steps: Identify each page or document in the fixed scope and the default human language of its complete content.
Inspect the page-level language declaration in markup, HTTP metadata, or the equivalent mechanism supported by the content technology.
Treat language changes within passages or phrases as a separate SC 3.1.2 review; they do not determine the SC 3.1.1 result.
procedure_steps: Determine the default human language of the page from its complete content rather than from a single phrase, navigation label, or locale setting.
Inspect the programmatically determinable page-level language and confirm that it identifies that default human language with a valid language value.
When the page is embedded, generated, or delivered through a non-HTML technology, inspect the equivalent page-level language mechanism supported by that technology.
Record the observed default language, the declared value and location, and any mismatch; do not convert correct or missing language-of-parts markup into an SC 3.1.1 result.
expected_results: The default human language of each scoped page can be programmatically determined.
The page-level declaration matches the default language of the page's complete content and uses a valid value for the content technology.
Language changes within parts remain explicitly outside this procedure and are handed to SC 3.1.2 when that criterion is in scope.
cant_tell_when: The review environment does not expose either the complete page content or the programmatic page-level language.
A generated or embedded document cannot be opened in a state where its default language and equivalent language metadata can both be inspected.

pass: An English page declares `lang="en"` on its root element, matching the default language of the complete page.
A primarily Japanese page includes some English product names but correctly declares Japanese as the page default.
fail: A page whose default human language is Japanese has no programmatically determinable page-level language.
A page whose complete content is primarily French declares English as its page-level language.
cant_tell: Only a partial screenshot is available, so neither the default language of the complete page nor its page-level metadata can be determined.

procedures.ai_boundary: AI may inventory candidate language boundaries and draft questions, but it must not record a profile outcome, human_verified mapping, or E2+ claim; an external human reviewer records any criterion result with target-specific evidence.

applicability_steps: Identify blocks of content that repeat across a set of pages in the fixed scope, such as shared navigation, headers, search regions, or repeated link groups.
Select representative pages from each materially different template or repeated-block pattern in the scoped page set.
Inventory every available mechanism for bypassing each repeated block, including skip links, structural headings, landmarks or regions, and other technology-supported mechanisms.
procedure_steps: For each repeated block, identify at least one available mechanism that lets a user bypass it and reach the content following that block.

Exercise operable skip controls with the input method they support, and inspect structural mechanisms such as headings or regions through a browser or assistive-technology navigation view as appropriate.
Repeat the review on representative pages from each applicable template and confirm that the mechanism remains available where the block repeats.
Record the repeated block, the mechanism used, its destination or navigation effect, and any page-set boundary; do not require a skip link when another sufficient mechanism is present.
expected_results: A mechanism is available to bypass each block of content that repeats across the scoped set of pages.
The available mechanism exposes or reaches the content following the repeated block without requiring the user to traverse the whole block again.
The evidence identifies which page set and repeated block were tested and which bypass mechanism satisfied the criterion.
cant_tell_when: The reviewer cannot inspect or operate the available bypass mechanism using the navigation mode for which that mechanism is provided.
The scoped page set or runtime personalization cannot be fixed well enough to determine which content blocks repeat across pages.

pass: A "Skip to main content" control is present as the first focus target and moves focus directly to the main article heading.
Pages use a consistent heading and landmark structure that lets assistive-technology users move past repeated navigation to the following content.
fail: A navigation block repeats across the scoped page set and no skip control, heading, region, or other bypass mechanism is available.
A skip link is present, but activating it leaves the user within the same repeated navigation block and no other bypass mechanism exists.
cant_tell: A dynamic application exposes navigation in a private script-only shell and no deterministic browseable state can be observed to identify repetitive blocks.

procedures.ai_boundary: AI may inventory repeated blocks and candidate bypass controls, but it must not record a profile outcome, human_verified mapping, or E2+ claim; an external human reviewer records any criterion result with target-specific evidence.

applicability_steps: Enumerate controls in the fixed scope for which the content requires user input, including text entry, selections, uploads, and task-specific data entry.
For each applicable control, identify the label or instructions needed to understand what input is requested and any required format, value, unit, or completion constraint.
Exclude controls for which no user input is required, and record related programmatic-association or error-handling questions separately under their applicable criteria.
procedure_steps: Inspect each applicable input request and confirm that a visible or otherwise user-available label or instruction identifies the requested input.
Confirm that instructions communicate constraints users must know before entering or choosing a value, such as a required format, range, unit, accepted file type, or required fields.

Check the control in its normal entry state and any state where the original instruction could disappear; placeholder-only text is insufficient when it vanishes during entry and no equivalent instruction remains.

Record programmatic label relationships, error identification, and error suggestions as separate evidence for SC 1.3.1, SC 4.1.2, SC 3.3.1, or SC 3.3.3 rather than making them extra pass conditions here.
expected_results: Labels or instructions are provided when content requires user input.
The supplied information communicates the input purpose and any constraints a user must know to complete the field or control.
A criterion result does not depend on satisfying separate programmatic-association or error-correction criteria.
cant_tell_when: The input request and its user-visible label or instructions cannot be observed together in the permitted review environment.
A required entry state cannot be reached, so the reviewer cannot determine which instructions are available when input is requested.

pass: A date field is labelled and gives the required YYYY-MM-DD format before entry.
A required upload field identifies its purpose and states the accepted file types and size limit.
fail: A phone-number field requests input but provides neither a label nor the format needed by the service.
An input uses placeholder text as the sole instruction, and the placeholder disappears before input without preserving equivalent help text.
cant_tell: The form renders via canvas and the reviewer cannot inspect control-label relationships or instruction text in a reliable target state.

procedures.ai_boundary: AI may inventory candidate controls and draft question lists, but it must not record a profile outcome, human_verified mapping, or E2+ claim; an external human reviewer records any criterion result with target-specific evidence.

applicability_steps: Identify text in the fixed scope, excluding captions and images of text from this criterion's required 200 percent resize test.
Determine a user-controlled text-resize or browser mechanism that reaches 200 percent without requiring assistive technology.
Record the initial viewport, zoom or text-size setting, content state, and any widgets whose text changes only after interaction.
procedure_steps: Increase the applicable text to 200 percent using the selected user-controlled mechanism, without relying on assistive technology.
Inspect all scoped text and text-bearing controls at that setting and exercise representative tasks to determine whether content or functionality is lost.

Record clipping, overlap, disappearance, truncation, or inoperable controls only when they cause loss of content or functionality; fixed pixel units or horizontal scrolling are not automatic failures of this criterion.
Separate captions and images of text from the required result, and record reflow or two-dimensional-scrolling issues separately under SC 1.4.10 when applicable.
expected_results: Text content can be enlarged to the required threshold without loss of content, functionality, or task context.
No essential information or controls become unavailable due solely to scale-related overflow, overlap, or clipping.
Captions and images of text are excluded from the required result, and related reflow findings are not substituted for this criterion.
cant_tell_when: The environment blocks browser zoom or text scaling control while preserving page state for inspection.
A locked rendering surface (e.g., immutable canvas output) prevents direct inspection of text layout after scale changes.

pass: At 200% text size, paragraph and control labels reflow without clipping and no essential text is lost.
At 200% browser zoom, some horizontal scrolling is needed, but all applicable text and controls remain available and functional; reflow is assessed separately.
fail: Scaled content overlaps controls so that the user cannot activate a required form element.
At 200% equivalent text size, long labels truncate behind container boundaries and hidden text contains required action instructions.
cant_tell: The page uses an inaccessible third-party renderer that locks scale and prevents confirmation of reflow behavior in the target scope.

procedures.ai_boundary: AI may inventory scaling-sensitive layout areas and draft checklists, but it must not record a profile outcome, human_verified mapping, or E2+ claim; an external human reviewer records any criterion result with target-specific evidence.

applicability_steps: Fix the review scope and inventory every user-operable function available within it, including controls, composite widgets, drag or drawing interactions, and state-dependent actions.
Identify the permitted interactive states needed to expose each function and record any state that cannot be reached without a pointer or other unavailable input.

Identify any function whose underlying purpose depends on the path of the user's movement rather than only its endpoints, and require a specific rationale before treating that path-dependent function as an exception.
procedure_steps: Enter each required permitted state and exercise every applicable function through a keyboard interface only, without using a pointer or mouse emulation as the substitute test.
For each exercise, record the starting state, exact keys and sequence used, observed result, and any function or state that remains unreachable.

Check whether operation requires a particular timing for individual keystrokes; where a path-dependent exception is claimed, record the underlying function, required movement path, and why endpoints alone cannot perform it.

Record keyboard traps, character-key shortcuts, focus visibility, focus order, and related issues separately under their own criteria; use them here only when they also show that functionality cannot be operated through a keyboard interface.
expected_results: Every applicable function in the fixed scope and permitted interactive states can be operated through a keyboard interface without requiring specific timings for individual keystrokes.
Any excluded path-dependent function has a recorded rationale showing that its underlying purpose depends on the movement path and not merely the endpoints.
The review evidence identifies the keys used, the observed result, and any unreachable function rather than inferring operability from the presence of keyboard event handlers.
cant_tell_when: The interactive runtime, a required interactive state, or the keyboard path needed to exercise an applicable function cannot be reached in the permitted environment.
A claimed path-dependent exception cannot be exercised or its underlying movement-path dependency cannot be distinguished from endpoint-only operation.

pass: A custom menu can be opened, traversed, activated, and closed with documented keys in every permitted menu state without per-keystroke timing.

A freehand drawing function lacks keyboard operation, but the reviewer verifies and records that the function inherently depends on the path of the user's movement rather than only start and end points.
fail: A file picker opens with the keyboard, but one available file action can be completed only with a pointer.
A control recognizes a key only when it is pressed within a narrow timing window, even though the underlying function does not depend on movement path.
cant_tell: The reviewer can see a state-dependent editor control but cannot enter the required state or send the keyboard sequence in the permitted runtime.

procedures.ai_boundary: AI may inventory candidate functions, states, or keyboard paths and draft review questions, but it must not record a profile outcome, human_verified mapping, or E2+ claim; an external human reviewer records any criterion result with target-specific keyboard and manual evidence.

applicability_steps: Inventory native and custom user interface components in the fixed scope, including components that appear only after permitted interaction or in a changed state.

For each component, identify its visible purpose, expected role, every applicable user-settable value, state, or property, and the assistive-technology, accessibility API, or equivalent accessibility-interface control path that can request each setting.

Identify components whose DOM or accessibility-tree exposure, applicable programmatic-set control path, or change behavior cannot be inspected in the permitted environment, and keep status-message-only behavior under SC 4.1.3 outside this procedure.
procedure_steps: Before interaction, inspect each native and custom component in the DOM and accessibility tree and record its programmatic name, role, and current user-settable values, states, or properties.
Perform each permitted interaction, then inspect the DOM and accessibility tree after the change and compare the exposed name, role, value, state, and property with the component's visible behavior.

For every applicable user-settable value, state, or property, use assistive technology, an accessibility API client, or an equivalent accessibility interface to attempt to programmatically set a distinct permitted setting through that interface.

Before each programmatic-set attempt, record the current value, state, or property and the requested setting; record the resulting value, state, or property after the attempt, whether the requested setting took effect, and the programmatic and visible observations.
Separately observe whether each change is exposed and notified to user agents, including assistive technology, and record the prior exposure, changed exposure, and notification observed.
Record status-message-only behavior separately under SC 4.1.3; do not use a status message by itself as evidence for this component name, role, value, state, or property procedure.
expected_results: Each applicable component exposes a programmatically determinable name and role that match its purpose in the reviewed state.

Every applicable user-settable value, state, or property accepts the requested permitted setting through assistive technology, an accessibility API, or an equivalent accessibility interface and exposes the resulting setting.
Changes to applicable values, states, and properties are separately exposed and notified to user agents, including assistive technology.
Native and custom components preserve accurate programmatic exposure before and after each permitted interaction.
cant_tell_when: The component's accessibility-tree exposure, interactive behavior, or assistive-technology notification cannot be observed in the permitted environment.
No applicable assistive-technology, accessibility API, or equivalent accessibility-interface control path is available to issue and observe a programmatic set operation.
A required state or change cannot be triggered, so the reviewer cannot compare the component before and after interaction.

pass: An accessibility API set request programmatically sets a custom slider from 20 to 40, the resulting value is exposed as 40, and the change notification is announced to assistive technology.
A custom disclosure exposes its label and button role, accepts an assistive-technology request to set its expanded state, exposes the requested resulting state, and notifies the state change.
fail: A custom toggle's changed state is exposed and its notification is announced after pointer operation, but an accessibility API set request fails and the state cannot be programmatically set through the accessibility interface.
An icon-only custom control performs an action but has no programmatically determinable name describing its purpose.
cant_tell: A custom control's value is visible in the accessibility tree, but no permitted assistive-technology or accessibility API control path is available to issue and observe a set request.

procedures.ai_boundary: AI may inventory candidate components, compare captured DOM or accessibility-tree states, or draft review questions, but it must not record a profile outcome, human_verified mapping, or E2+ claim; an external human reviewer records any criterion result with target-specific browser and assistive-technology evidence.

applicability_steps: Identify keyboard-focusable components in the fixed page states, viewport, zoom, and author-created sticky or overlay content.
Record the initial position of user-movable content and whether user-opened content can be dismissed or moved without advancing keyboard focus.
procedure_steps: Move keyboard focus through each applicable component, including controls near sticky headers, footers, notifications, and persistent overlays; record the focused component and viewport state.
At each focus stop, inspect whether author-created content entirely hides the component itself. If user-opened content covers it, try the available reveal action without advancing focus.
Repeat in the scoped responsive or zoomed state. Record any obscuring layer and distinguish component visibility from separate focus-indicator visibility under 2.4.7.
expected_results: Every keyboard-focused component remains at least partly visible, or user-opened content can reveal it without advancing focus.
User-movable content is checked in its initial position; unrelated focus-indicator appearance is assessed separately.
cant_tell_when: Keyboard focus, the component boundary, or the author-created obscuring layer cannot be observed in a permitted target state.
The initial position or focus-preserving reveal behavior of user-movable or user-opened content cannot be established.

pass: A focused link under a sticky header remains partly visible, and the user can identify the focused component.
fail: A persistent cookie banner entirely covers a keyboard-focused button and cannot be dismissed without moving focus.
cant_tell: A screenshot shows an overlay, but there is no keyboard-focus trace identifying which component is focused beneath it.

procedures.ai_boundary: AI may flag candidate overlays and focus paths, but it must not record a profile outcome, human_verified mapping, or E2+ claim; an external human reviewer verifies component visibility in the fixed target states.

applicability_steps: Identify input workflows that automatically detect omitted required information, invalid formats or values, or automatically corrected input.
Choose permitted, non-sensitive test data that triggers each relevant detected-error state; do not infer an error state where the target does not detect one.
procedure_steps: Trigger each applicable detected error through the permitted form or input flow, and record the submitted value, field, detection point, and resulting page state.
Inspect the user-facing text for both the identity of the item in error and a description of what is wrong; repeat for multiple simultaneous errors when the flow permits.
Check whether automatically corrected input is described to the user. Record correction suggestions under 3.3.3 and programmatic name or state exposure under their separate criteria.
expected_results: For every automatically detected input error, text identifies the affected item and describes the error.
A failed submission does more than silently redisplay the form, and an automatic correction is described to the user.
cant_tell_when: The error state cannot be safely triggered with permitted test data, or the resulting text and affected item cannot be observed.
The reviewer cannot determine whether a changed value was an automatic correction or a user action.

pass: After an invalid date is submitted, text identifies the Date field and states that its value is outside the allowed range.
fail: Submission fails and the form reappears with a red border only; no text identifies the erroneous field or describes the error.
cant_tell: A form is shown in a screenshot after submission, but the submitted values and validation result were not captured.

procedures.ai_boundary: AI may draft safe error cases and inventory visible messages, but it must not record a profile outcome, human_verified mapping, or E2+ claim; an external human reviewer triggers and evaluates each relevant error state.

applicability_steps: Identify vertically and horizontally scrolling content in the fixed page; record reading direction, starting viewport, and zoom.
Identify only sections that require two-dimensional layout for use or meaning, such as a data table or map; do not extend that exception to surrounding text.
procedure_steps: Present vertically scrolling content at a width equivalent to 320 CSS pixels, or horizontally scrolling content at a height equivalent to 256 CSS pixels; record effective dimensions.

Read and operate each non-excepted section in the constrained view, including navigation, forms, controls, and responsive variants; record information loss, clipping, and any need for two-dimensional scrolling.
For a claimed exception, inspect the smallest section that needs two-dimensional layout and confirm surrounding content still reflows; assess text resizing under 1.4.4 separately.
expected_results: Non-excepted sections retain information and functionality without two-dimensional scrolling at the applicable equivalent dimension.
Any two-dimensional layout exception is limited to the section whose use or meaning requires it.
cant_tell_when: The effective viewport, scrolling direction, or constrained state cannot be established.
A claimed exception or affected functionality cannot be inspected in the permitted target.

pass: A data table scrolls within its own region at 320 CSS pixels while adjacent paragraphs and controls remain readable and operable without horizontal page scrolling.
fail: At 320 CSS pixels a paragraph and submit control extend beyond the viewport, requiring both horizontal and vertical scrolling to read and operate them.
cant_tell: A narrow screenshot shows a scrollbar but not its container, affected section, or whether information and controls remain available.

procedures.ai_boundary: AI may flag overflow candidates and record viewport measurements, but it must not classify an exception or record a profile outcome, human_verified mapping, or E2+ claim; a human reviewer checks reading and operation.

applicability_steps: Identify updates reporting an action result, waiting state, progress, or error without changing context or moving focus.
Separate status messages from focused dialogs, page navigation, ordinary result content, and component value changes assessed under other criteria.
procedure_steps: Trigger representative status updates, including a repeated update when available, and record visible text, focus, timing, and the resulting accessibility-tree state.
Inspect the role or properties that make the message programmatically determinable without focus; check that the exposed text gives enough context rather than an isolated changing number.
Where the target screen reader is available, record its actual announcement separately from programmatic exposure; otherwise keep speech unverified.
expected_results: Applicable status messages are programmatically determinable through role or properties without receiving focus.
The update conveys its result, waiting state, progress, or error in context; an unrelated focus change does not substitute for status semantics.
cant_tell_when: The status state cannot be triggered or its role, properties, and message text cannot be observed.
The reviewer cannot determine whether the change is a status message or a change of context.

pass: After search, focus stays on the search control and a status reading '5 results returned' is exposed through an appropriate role or property.
fail: After saving, a visible 'Saved' message appears without a role or property that exposes it as a status update.
cant_tell: A screenshot shows 'Saved', but the trigger, focus behavior, and accessibility-tree state were not captured.

procedures.ai_boundary: AI may inventory status candidates and inspect captured roles or properties, but it must not infer actual speech or record a profile outcome, human_verified mapping, or E2+ claim; a human reviewer evaluates the update.

applicability_steps: Identify keyboard-sequential navigation paths and states in the fixed scope where order affects meaning or operation.
Include controls revealed by dialogs, menus, validation, or other state changes; distinguish sequential navigation from a component's arrow-key navigation.
procedure_steps: Traverse each relevant state with the keyboard's sequential focus command, recording the focused component, prior component, and nearby content at each transition.
Compare the observed order with the relationships and tasks conveyed in the page; test entry into and exit from dynamic regions and return from dialogs.

Record where an order breaks meaning or operation; do not fail merely because focus differs from visual or DOM order when a logical usable order remains. Assess focus visibility under 2.4.7 separately.
expected_results: Where sequential order matters, a keyboard user can encounter and operate components in an order that preserves meaning and operability.
At least one logical order is sufficient; identical visual and focus sequences are not required.
cant_tell_when: The relevant interactive state or sequential keyboard path cannot be reached in the permitted environment.
A focus transition is observed without enough surrounding content to judge its effect on meaning or operation.

pass: A dialog opens from its trigger, its controls receive focus in a usable order, and closing it returns focus to the trigger or next logical control.
fail: Tab moves repeatedly between unrelated form sections, separating each field from the instructions needed to complete it.
cant_tell: A DOM snapshot lists tabindex values, but the actual keyboard path and dynamic states were not exercised.

procedures.ai_boundary: AI may list focusable elements or proposed paths, but it must not infer a profile outcome, human_verified mapping, or E2+ claim from DOM order alone; a human reviewer traverses the relevant states.

applicability_steps: Identify keyboard-operable controls and the available keyboard operation modes in the fixed target states.
Include controls introduced by dynamic content; distinguish indicator visibility from focus order, obstruction, and non-text contrast reviews.
procedure_steps: Move keyboard focus through representative controls in each relevant mode and state; record the focused control and the visible change that identifies it.
Observe whether the indicator persists while focus stays on the control, including after a short wait or state update.
For a suspected missing indicator, verify actual focus and whether another keyboard operation mode visibly indicates it; record contrast or obscuration concerns under their separate criteria.
expected_results: Every keyboard-operable interface has a mode in which its keyboard focus indicator is visible on the focused control.
The visible focus indication remains while keyboard focus stays on that control.
cant_tell_when: The reviewer cannot establish which control has keyboard focus or cannot access the relevant operation mode.
The focus state disappears before its indicator can be observed or the target rendering cannot be inspected.

pass: Tab moves to a button and a visible outline remains until focus moves away.
fail: A keyboard-focused button has no visible indicator in any available operation mode.
cant_tell: A still image shows an outline, but the keyboard path and actual focused control are unknown.

procedures.ai_boundary: AI may flag CSS or captured focus-state candidates, but it must not record a profile outcome, human_verified mapping, or E2+ claim from styles alone; a human reviewer verifies the visible indicator during keyboard operation.

applicability_steps: Identify every scoped component that can receive keyboard focus, including embedded content, editors, dialogs, popovers, and their reachable states.
Record the keyboard interface, browser, operating system, and entry path; a deliberate focus cycle inside an open dialog is not by itself a failure if users can leave it by keyboard.
procedure_steps: Enter each representative component using only the keyboard interface, then try to move focus away with Tab, Shift+Tab, arrow keys where relevant, and the standard exit methods of the tested environment.
For a dialog or other contained region, test its keyboard dismissal or exit controls and confirm that focus can leave the region; record the actual key sequence and resulting focus destination.
If leaving requires a nonstandard key sequence, inspect whether the user is advised of that method when needed and verify that it works without a pointing device.
Assess whether all functionality is keyboard operable under SC 2.1.1 and whether the subsequent focus order preserves meaning under SC 2.4.3 separately.
expected_results: Every component reached by keyboard permits focus to move away through the keyboard interface in the tested state, including after entering embedded or modal content.
When the exit requires more than ordinary arrow, Tab, or other standard methods for that environment, the user receives usable instructions for the exit method.
cant_tell_when: The component or trapped state cannot be reached, or the focused destination cannot be observed in the permitted runtime.
The available keyboard interface or platform-specific standard exit method is unknown, or the alleged nonstandard exit instruction cannot be inspected.

pass: A modal cycles focus among its controls while open, and its keyboard-operable Cancel control closes it and returns focus to the page.
fail: An embedded editor captures Tab and other tested exit keys, offers no usable keyboard exit, and leaves focus inside the editor.
cant_tell: A screenshot shows an open modal, but no keyboard entry, exit attempt, or resulting focus position was observed.

procedures.ai_boundary: AI may identify focusable components and candidate exit instructions, but it must not infer a profile outcome, human_verified mapping, or E2+ claim from markup alone; a human reviewer tests entry and exit with the relevant keyboard interface.

applicability_steps: Identify user-input errors automatically detected in the fixed form or process, including omitted required values and values outside an accepted format or set.
For each detected error, determine whether a usable correction is known; record a specific security or content-purpose reason before applying the criterion's exception.
procedure_steps: Using safe test values, trigger representative automatically detected errors and record the field, rejected input, validation state, and guidance shown to the user.

Compare each known correction rule with the post-error guidance; check whether it tells the user how to repair the input, such as an accepted format or valid choice, rather than only saying that the value is invalid.
For a claimed security or purpose exception, inspect the particular information that a suggestion would expose or the task it would defeat; do not treat every sensitive form as exempt.
Assess textual identification of the wrong item under SC 3.3.1, instructions available before input under SC 3.3.2, and prevention or confirmation under SC 3.3.4 separately.
expected_results: When an input error is detected automatically and a safe correction is known, the user receives a suggestion that can guide a valid correction.
Withholding a known suggestion is limited to a demonstrated security or content-purpose conflict; an error label alone does not substitute for correction guidance.
cant_tell_when: The validation state cannot be triggered or the guidance after detection cannot be observed in the permitted target.
The accepted rule, availability of a safe correction, or the claimed security or purpose conflict cannot be established.

pass: After a date in an unsupported format is rejected, the field's error guidance gives the accepted date format and the user can correct the value.
fail: A form rejects a known invalid date format but displays only 'Invalid value' although the accepted format could safely be stated.
cant_tell: A static form image shows a format hint, but no automatically detected error or resulting guidance was observed.

procedures.ai_boundary: AI may list validation rules and candidate suggestions from captured evidence, but it must not decide whether an exception applies or record a profile outcome, human_verified mapping, or E2+ claim; a human reviewer tests the error state and its guidance.

applicability_steps: Inventory visible text and images of text in the fixed states, including placeholders and text revealed on hover or keyboard focus.
Classify ordinary versus large-scale text using its actual size and weight; record any claimed inactive, decorative, invisible, incidental-picture, or logotype exception with its context.
procedure_steps: For each applicable text sample, inspect the effective foreground and adjacent background colors in the tested state, including transparency or changing backgrounds; use the specified or computed colors rather than anti-aliased edge pixels for DOM text, and record colors, size, weight, and ratio.

Compare the unrounded ratio with 4.5:1 for ordinary text or 3:1 for large-scale text; assess large-scale status at the delivered size against 18 pt regular, 14 pt bold, or equivalent CJK sizing rather than appearance alone.
Check images of text and state-dependent text as text. Do not classify essential graphical marks or component boundaries under this criterion; assess those separately under SC 1.4.11.
Review claimed exceptions item by item; a brand style outside an actual logotype and text in an operable control do not inherit the logo or inactive-control exception.
expected_results: Applicable ordinary text and images of text reach at least 4.5:1 against their effective backgrounds, without rounding a lower result upward.
Applicable large-scale text reaches at least 3:1, and any lower-contrast item has a documented exception that applies to that item.
cant_tell_when: The actual foreground or background in the relevant state cannot be established, such as text over an unobserved changing image.
Font size or weight, image-of-text classification, or a claimed exception cannot be verified from the available target evidence.

pass: Ordinary button text measures 4.7:1 against its rendered background in the tested enabled state.
fail: Ordinary instructional text measures 4.49:1; rounding the displayed value to 4.5:1 does not meet the threshold.
cant_tell: A screenshot shows light text over a photo, but the effective background under the letters and the text size were not established.

procedures.ai_boundary: AI may flag candidate color pairs and calculate provisional ratios, but it must not infer applicable exceptions or record a profile outcome, human_verified mapping, or E2+ claim from a scanner result alone; a human reviewer verifies the rendered state and measurements.

applicability_steps: Inventory visual cues needed to identify operable user interface components or their states, including icon-only controls, selection marks, and authored focus indicators in reachable states.

Identify parts of graphics needed to understand the content; record equivalent visible information and any claimed inactive-control, unmodified user-agent, or essential-presentation exception for the particular item.
procedure_steps: Inspect each required non-text cue in its actual state and identify the adjacent colors needed to distinguish it. A control boundary need not be tested when another sufficient visual cue identifies the control; review text contrast under SC 1.4.3 separately.

Record the cue, state, effective adjacent colors, and unrounded contrast ratio. Account for transparency, gradients, and varying backgrounds, and compare the required cue against its adjacent color or colors at the 3:1 threshold.

For informative graphics, test only the parts needed to understand the content, such as a necessary chart line or symbol; verify whether visible labels or another available presentation already convey the same information.

Review exceptions item by item: confirm that an inactive component cannot currently be operated, that an exempt native appearance is determined by the user agent and unmodified by the author, or that changing a particular graphic presentation would undermine its meaning. Do not require a 3:1 change between nonadjacent states of one component.
expected_results: Required visual cues for applicable components and their states distinguish themselves from adjacent colors at 3:1 or higher in the tested states.
Each graphical part required for understanding reaches 3:1 against adjacent colors, unless a documented exception applies to that particular presentation.
cant_tell_when: The relevant component state, graphic, or effective adjacent colors cannot be observed or established in the permitted target.
The evidence does not establish whether a cue is required, equivalent information is available, or a claimed inactive, user-agent, or essential-presentation exception applies.

pass: A required selected-state checkmark measures 3.2:1 against its adjacent fill in the tested state.
fail: An icon is the only visible cue identifying an active button, but it measures 2.7:1 against its adjacent background.
cant_tell: A screenshot shows a pale chart line, but the underlying data labels and actual adjacent colors cannot be inspected.

procedures.ai_boundary: AI may identify candidate cues and calculate provisional color ratios, but it must not decide whether a cue is required, an exception applies, or a profile outcome, human_verified mapping, or E2+ claim follows from a scanner result alone; a human reviewer verifies the actual states and visual meaning.

applicability_steps: Identify meaningful color differences in the fixed content and reachable states, including links, required or erroneous fields, status cues, charts, and instructions referring to a color.
For each color-coded meaning, identify the intended information, action, response, or visual distinction and any visible cue available to a sighted user who cannot distinguish the colors.
procedure_steps: Inspect representative default and changed states in their context. For each meaning encoded by color, check whether visible text, a symbol, pattern, shape, underline, or other non-hue cue conveys the same meaning without relying on the color name alone.

Where the additional distinction is lightness rather than text or shape, verify at least 3:1 between the relevant colors and that the user need not identify which specific hue denotes a meaning; compare the actual paired states or chart categories, not merely each color against the page background.

Check that an accessible name or hidden text alone has not been mistaken for the visible alternative required by this criterion. Assess programmatic relationships under SC 1.3.1, text contrast under SC 1.4.3, and required non-text cue contrast under SC 1.4.11 separately.

If the only suspected color difference marks a link's visited history, apply the W3C Understanding guidance for that browser-controlled state rather than treating it as an ordinary author-defined status cue.
expected_results: Every meaning or action communicated through an author-controlled color difference remains visually distinguishable through an adequate non-hue cue or a sufficient lightness difference where the specific hue is not itself required.
A user can identify color-coded form states, links, and graphical categories in the tested context without needing to name or distinguish their hues.
cant_tell_when: The relevant color-coded state or its surrounding context cannot be reached or observed in the permitted target.
The meaning assigned to the colors, visibility of an alternative cue, or effective colors needed to assess a claimed lightness distinction cannot be established.

pass: A required field uses red styling and a visible required marker explained next to the form.
fail: A chart identifies two data series only as red and green, without labels, patterns, or a sufficient lightness distinction.
cant_tell: A cropped image shows red and green field borders, but the labels and validation messages outside the crop are unavailable.

procedures.ai_boundary: AI may flag color-coded candidates and provisional luminance comparisons, but it must not infer that a visible alternative conveys the same meaning or record a profile outcome, human_verified mapping, or E2+ claim from CSS or an accessibility-tree label alone; a human reviewer checks the rendered context.

applicability_steps: Identify scoped pages and final actions that create a legal commitment or financial transaction, modify or delete stored user-controllable data, or submit a user's test responses; record what becomes final and who can control the affected data.

Use a permitted test account or non-production fixture to inspect consequential actions. If no safe path exists, review pre-final states and available records without submitting a real transaction, deletion, or test response.
procedure_steps: For each applicable action, trace the user flow up to finalization and identify whether it offers a reversible submission, checks entered data for input errors with an opportunity to correct them, or provides review, confirmation, and correction before finalization.

For a reversible route, verify the usable undo or cancellation method and its applicable time or conditions in a safe test flow; a vague claim that staff may help later is not sufficient without an effective reversal path.

For a checked route, use safe values to trigger representative rejected input and confirm that the user can correct it before the consequential action completes. Record error identification under SC 3.3.1 and suggestions under SC 3.3.3 separately.
For a confirmed route, inspect the information or action presented before finalization, then verify that the user can review and confirm it and has a way to correct it before the final action.
expected_results: Each applicable consequential submission has at least one working safeguard: reversible, checked with correction, or reviewable and correctable before final confirmation.
The safeguard operates at the point where the action becomes consequential, and the reviewer records which of the three routes supports the finding.
cant_tell_when: The consequence of the final action or whether affected stored data is user-controllable cannot be established from the permitted target and records.
No safe path or adequate evidence is available to verify the claimed reversal, correction, or pre-final review mechanism without causing a real transaction, deletion, or test submission.

pass: Before placing a test order, a summary shows the items, quantity, and payment choice; the user can return to correct them or cancel before final confirmation.
fail: Submitting an account deletion immediately removes stored user-controllable records, with no effective undo, checked correction path, or pre-final review and correction.
cant_tell: A live purchase page promises later cancellation, but the cancellation terms and a safe test path are unavailable.

procedures.ai_boundary: AI may identify candidate consequential flows and safeguards, but it must not infer that a transaction is reversible or a correction mechanism works from labels alone, or record a profile outcome, human_verified mapping, or E2+ claim without a human review of the permitted flow.

applicability_steps: Map each scoped multi-step process, including required steps on another domain, and identify information the user previously entered or the process provided that is requested again in the same activity.

Distinguish a continuous process from a later session or separate activity; record any item-specific claim that re-entry is essential, required for security, or necessary because the earlier value is no longer valid.
procedure_steps: Using safe test values, move through the process and record the first entry or presentation of each item and the later point where the same information is required again.

At each repeated request, check whether the content auto-populates the value or makes the previous value available for selection on the current page, such as a same-address control or selectable text; do not count browser autocomplete alone.
If a repeated request remains, verify the specific essential, security, or invalid-value reason. Do not treat all password, personal, or payment fields as automatically exempt.

Record whether the repeated request is part of an error-recovery step or a third-party handoff within the same process; assess input instructions and error feedback under SC 3.3.2 and SC 3.3.1 separately.
expected_results: Information previously entered or provided in the same process is not required again unless it is auto-populated or available for the user to select.
Each remaining re-entry requirement has an item-specific essential, security, or invalid-previous-value reason supported by the observed process.
cant_tell_when: The reviewer cannot reach the earlier and repeated request in one permitted process, including a required third-party step.
The earlier value, selection mechanism, or claimed essential, security, or invalid-value reason cannot be established from the available evidence.

pass: A checkout form offers a selectable 'same as shipping address' option when billing address is requested later in the same process.
fail: The checkout repeats the corporate ID entered two steps earlier and requires typing it again, with no supplied value or applicable exception.
cant_tell: Only the final payment page is available; the earlier entry and whether the same value can be selected are unknown.

procedures.ai_boundary: AI may map repeated prompts and candidate exceptions, but it must not infer that values can be selected or an exception applies from field names alone, or record a profile outcome, human_verified mapping, or E2+ claim without a human review of the same process.

applicability_steps: Map authentication of an existing account in the fixed scope, including sign-in, required second factors, reauthentication, recovery authentication, and challenges that appear only after an error or risk signal; distinguish initial account creation.

At each required step, identify any memory, transcription, calculation, or puzzle task and the claimed alternative, assisting mechanism, object-recognition exception, or recognition of user-provided non-text content.
procedure_steps: With an authorized test account and safe test values, follow each reachable authentication path and record the required steps, conditional challenges, available alternatives, and the point where the user can continue without a cognitive function test.

For credentials and verification codes, check whether a password manager or user agent can fill the input, or whether the complete value can be pasted from the clipboard without forced retyping, splitting, or character extraction. Do not assume that a field attribute alone proves the mechanism works.

For a claimed alternative, verify that the complete path is available and avoids an unassisted cognitive function test at every required step. For a claimed AA exception, confirm that the task is object recognition or identifying non-text content previously provided by the user, rather than a text transcription or a puzzle beyond recognition.

Record account recovery and conditionally triggered CAPTCHA separately. Assess input-purpose semantics under SC 1.3.5, control names under SC 4.1.2, and the stricter AAA authentication requirement under SC 3.3.9 separately.
expected_results: Every required authentication step has a usable route without an unassisted cognitive function test, or meets one of the two specific recognition exceptions allowed at AA level.
Where copy/paste or autofill is the assisting mechanism, the relevant complete credential or code can actually be entered without recall or transcription in the tested flow.
cant_tell_when: No authorized test account or safe route is available to inspect a required second factor, recovery step, or conditional challenge without exposing real credentials or changing a live account.
A claimed alternative, assisting mechanism, or recognition exception cannot be exercised or its applicability cannot be established in the permitted target state.

pass: A test account's password can be filled by a password manager, and its required one-time code can be pasted in full; no later step forces memorization or transcription.
fail: A required one-time code must be typed digit by digit because pasting fills only the first box, and no other usable authentication route is offered.
cant_tell: The test account reaches the password step, but a risk-triggered challenge and recovery path cannot be reached safely, so the complete authentication process is unverified.

procedures.ai_boundary: AI may inventory authentication steps and candidate mechanisms, but it must not use real credentials, infer that autofill or alternatives work from markup alone, or record a profile outcome, human_verified mapping, or E2+ claim without a human review of the permitted authentication paths.

applicability_steps: Inventory author-controlled pointer targets in the fixed page and relevant responsive or revealed states, including icon buttons, links, map controls, and controls in overlays; record the tested viewport and input modality.

Identify actual clickable regions rather than visible glyph dimensions. Treat a slider, color gradient, or editable area where position selects a value as one target; note targets whose size is controlled only by the user agent.
procedure_steps: Inspect each target's rendered activation area in CSS pixels. Check whether an axis-aligned solid 24 by 24 CSS pixel square fits entirely inside it; a 24 by 24 bounding box alone does not prove this for rounded, clipped, or irregular shapes.

For an undersized target, center a 24 CSS pixel diameter circle on its bounding box and check that it intersects neither another target nor the circle of another undersized target in the same state. Use actual target areas, not merely visual gaps or keyboard access.

If spacing does not apply, verify a same-page control that performs the same function and itself meets this criterion, or check the specific inline, unmodified user-agent, essential-presentation, or legal-presentation exception. Do not exempt every small icon or map control by category.

Record the target, dimensions or measured geometry, nearby targets, state, and applicable route or exception. Assess pointer gesture alternatives under SC 2.5.1, dragging under SC 2.5.7, and the stricter 44 by 44 CSS pixel AAA size under SC 2.5.5 separately.
expected_results: Each applicable pointer target contains a 24 by 24 CSS pixel square, or its observed geometry and context support one of the five specific AA exceptions.
For a spacing or equivalent-control claim, the measured neighbors or the usable same-page control establish the exception in the tested state.
cant_tell_when: The pointer activation boundary or neighboring targets cannot be inspected in the relevant responsive or revealed state.
An asserted same-page equivalent, unmodified user-agent sizing, essential presentation, or legal requirement cannot be established from the permitted target and evidence.

pass: A 20 by 20 CSS pixel icon target has 4 CSS pixels of clear space from each adjacent undersized icon, and its 24-pixel circle intersects no other target or undersized circle.
fail: Two 18 by 18 CSS pixel toolbar buttons are adjacent with no qualifying spacing or same-page equivalent, although each icon has a keyboard shortcut.
cant_tell: A screenshot shows two small icons, but the clickable padding and neighboring target boundaries cannot be inspected.

procedures.ai_boundary: AI may flag small visible controls and estimate candidate geometry, but it must not infer the actual hit area, spacing, or an exception from a screenshot or CSS declaration alone, or record a profile outcome, human_verified mapping, or E2+ claim without a human review of the rendered target.
